1.1.rationale: The policy explicitly references domestic violence by citing the national law on the elimination of domestic violence in its legal basis, indicating the policy addresses domestic violence within its framework.

1.2.rationale: The policy explicitly lists sexual violence as a form of violence covered under its scope of protection for women and children.

1.3.rationale: The policy explicitly includes physical violence as one of the acts of violence from which women and children have the right to protection.

1.4.rationale: The policy explicitly includes psychological violence as a covered form of violence in its scope.

Article 2 Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
Article 3 Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. Letter b What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. Letter c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person.
Letter d What is meant by intimidation is the act of ordering or prohibiting by means of threatening or restraining to cause harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for their best interests.
Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is the act of ordering by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right possessed by a person to a place suitable for them. Letter f What is meant by deprivation of liberty is the act of eliminating the right to live based on the best interests of a person. Letter g What is meant by neglect is:
a. actions that result in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions that deliberately neglect to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate; c. actions that neglect a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

What is meant by "trafficking in persons" is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10 (1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11 (1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12 The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from relevant agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academicians and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13 (1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14 (1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements include:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15 (1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children in carrying out its functions builds a working network with: a. Police; b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Agency; e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with: a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of joint agreement.
Article 16 (1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities; b. provision of education and job training; c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17 The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.
2.1.rationale: The policy establishes an institutional arrangement (P2TP2A) and explicitly provides for building working networks and cooperation across jurisdictions, including with provincial and other regency/city governments, indicating intergovernmental coordination.

6.1.rationale: The provided passages discuss protection of women and children from violence generally (including prevention, services, empowerment, safe houses), but none explicitly mention conflict/disaster-prone areas or special measures for women in such contexts.

6.2.rationale: The cited passage explicitly includes “exploitation and human trafficking” within acts of violence from which women have a right to protection, and frames protection measures for women victims within the regulation’s scope.

6.3.rationale: None of the passages specifically mention women workers/employees or workplace-specific protections; the text focuses on violence against women and children in general.

6.4.rationale: The passages define women generally and provide general protections for women and children, but do not identify elderly women as a specific group or provide targeted measures for them.

6.5.rationale: The provided passages do not mention disability or persons with disabilities, nor do they set out disability-specific protection measures.

6.6.rationale: The passages do not mention women heads of household/families as a distinct target group or provide tailored protections for them.

6.7.rationale: While the regulation includes nondiscrimination as a principle, none of the passages specifically address women from minority or isolated groups or provide special measures targeted to them.

6.8.rationale: The passages provide legal assistance and accompaniment for victims, but do not specifically address women in conflict with the law as witnesses or perpetrators, nor provide protections tailored to those roles.

6.9.rationale: The passages do not mention Indigenous peoples/masyarakat adat as a protected group or provide any special measures targeted at them.

6.10.rationale: Although “forced eviction” is listed as a form of violence, the passages do not establish special protection measures specifically targeted at refugees or forcibly displaced persons as a group.

6.11.rationale: There is no specific mention of domestic workers or protections tailored to domestic work contexts; the regulation addresses violence against women and children generally.

6.12.rationale: The passages do not mention homelessness or women experiencing homelessness as a specific target group, nor do they provide homelessness-specific protection measures.

6.13.rationale: The passages do not mention former inmates/formerly incarcerated women or provide any targeted protections or reintegration measures specific to that group.

Article 21 (1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
Promulgated in Paringin on January 20, 2016 (2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

7.2.rationale: The provided passages identify funding from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and non-binding third-party grants/contributions, but do not mention any national government budget source.

7.3.rationale: While the text mentions possible cooperation with “international institutions whose existence is recognized,” it does not explicitly identify international donors or international funding as a budget source; the funding provision only refers to regional budget and non-binding third-party grants/contributions without specifying international sources.
